# Backchannel

> Backchannel is a self-hosted, open-source (MIT) AI meeting assistant. It
> captures meeting audio in the browser, builds a live speaker-attributed
> transcript using local voice activity detection and speaker embeddings,
> and runs configurable AI agents (Google Gemini or OpenAI, with optional
> fully local ONNX transcription) that surface questions, objections,
> opportunities, and action items while the meeting is still happening.

Backchannel is free to run: there is no hosted service, no pricing tiers,
and no account. You can run it from the desktop executable on Windows,
macOS, or Linux, or deploy it yourself with Docker Compose (React frontend,
FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL). Bring your own Gemini or OpenAI API key, or transcribe
fully offline with local ONNX Whisper/Parakeet models. Because it is
self-hosted, meeting audio and transcripts never leave your infrastructure
except for the model API calls you configure.

Key facts:
- License: MIT, source at https://github.com/talberthoule/backchannel
- Category: real-time meeting analysis / AI meeting assistant / meeting copilot
- Desktop release: Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Linux x64 downloads at https://downloads.backchannel.page/ for approved Backchannel accounts; no GitHub identity or repository membership is required
- Self-hosted alternative to cloud meeting assistants such as Otter.ai,
  Fireflies.ai, and Granola
- Stack: React 18 + TypeScript frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL 16
- Diarization: Silero VAD + WeSpeaker ResNet152 speaker embeddings (local, ONNX)
- Transcription: Gemini Flash, or fully offline ONNX Whisper/Parakeet
- Agents: consolidated analyst, objection handler, synthesizer, opportunity
  specialist -- each with a configurable model, prompt, and trigger
- Works with any meeting app: captures mic plus tab/system audio in the
  browser, so Zoom, Meet, and Teams need no bot or integration

## Docs

- [Download portal](https://downloads.backchannel.page/): authenticated Windows, macOS, and Linux executable delivery for approved Backchannel accounts
- [Desktop release v0.3.1](https://backchannel.page/releases/v0.3.1/): public asset inventory, release notes, install notes, and first-run guidance
- [Quickstart](https://backchannel.page/docs/quickstart/): Docker Compose setup, local development, migrations, tests
- [Architecture](https://backchannel.page/docs/architecture/): the live call path end to end
- [Agent System](https://backchannel.page/docs/agents/): each agent's trigger, purpose, and configuration
- [Audio Pipeline](https://backchannel.page/docs/audio-pipeline/): capture format, VAD/diarization, transcription routing
- [WebSocket Protocol](https://backchannel.page/docs/websocket-protocol/): binary audio framing and message types
- [REST API](https://backchannel.page/docs/rest-api/): endpoint reference
- [Configuration](https://backchannel.page/docs/configuration/): settings, environment variables, model registry
- [Deployment](https://backchannel.page/docs/deployment/): compose services, GPU support, startup behavior

## Compare

- [Open-source Otter.ai alternative](https://backchannel.page/otter-alternative/): self-hosted transcripts and insights without minute caps
- [Open-source Granola alternative](https://backchannel.page/granola-alternative/): bot-free capture, self-hosted and real-time
- [Fireflies.ai alternative without the bot](https://backchannel.page/fireflies-alternative/): live assistance on your own hardware
- [Backchannel vs Meetily](https://backchannel.page/vs-meetily/): two open-source meeting assistants compared
